newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve flattens over past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve flattens over past week - Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve flattened an average of five basis points for the second week in a row in the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
The flattening came amid price erosion for long-term bonds, while short-term yields held steady on the week.
The spread between one-year and 30-year bonds narrowed five basis points in the triple-A category for the third week in a row, leaving 185 basis points to separate one-year and 30-year munis.
The Baa yield curve between one-year and thirty-year bonds also flattened five, for the second consecutive week, to 190 basis points.
Average yields on one-year municipal bonds were unchanged across the credit spectrum, holding at 3.90 percent in the triple-A category and 4.70 percent on Baa's.

The intermediate sector was flat for the week, with Aaa-rated 10-year bond yields unchanged at 5.15 percent for the second consecutive week, and Baa-rated ten-years holding steady at six percent after rising five the week before.
Long-term municipals outperformed the Treasury market during the week.
The yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond rose six basis points by the close on Thursday, reversing the prior week's four basis point drop and finishing at 7.13 percent.
Thirty-year municipal yields, meanwhile, fell five basis points across the credit spectrum, moving to 5.75 percent for Aaa-rated bonds and 6.60 percent for 30-year Baa's.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 81 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 82 percent last week.

The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the second week in a row at 80 basis points. The 30-year spread was unchanged for the third consecutive week at 85 basis points.
